title: scenes.json
description: The window-scene data model (LEO-235). A scene is a named description of how matching windows behave on one named workspace: layout and layout options, grouping, per-class window properties (position, size, opacity, blur opt-out, group/float state), binding context, and the geometry divergence between desk-dual and laptop-solo. Scenes are keyed by name — the workspace's `default_name` — not by workspace id, because the same logical scene (gaming) sits on workspace 5 on laptop-solo and 4 on desk-dual. Which workspace id a scene runs on is host data: hyprland.lua's `workspace_specs` will gain a `scene` field binding a workspace id to a name, exactly as `monitor` already is a host-resolved sentinel rather than a scene property. The profile boundary (LEO-235) lives in `geometry`: the same scene can scroll the desk and fit-or-float the lid, even swap layouts (code is dwindled on desk-dual, monocled on laptop-solo). Consumers: the hypr event manager (layout_opts, solo_gaps, opacity, and the future scene re-evaluator) reads this through the mtime-cached store handle, and the workspace scene editor (LEO-239) edits it from the shell. Static behavior (grouping, workspace pinning) is generated at config load; geometry and layout options are reapplied reactively on the events a scene lists in `reevaluate_on`. Enforcement is deterministic: the current workspace selects the active scene, `members` matches the window set, and matching windows are addressed as one data set.

scenes.description: Scenes by name. The name is the workspace `default_name` (e.g. `code`, `gaming`, `media`) so a scene is host-independent; the host's `workspace_specs` binds a workspace id to it.

layout.description: The scene's base tiling layout. `monocle` is our own layout running on Hyprland's master algorithm (hypr/layouts/master.lua); the option namespaces are declared in hypr/events/layout_opts.lua. A profile listed under `geometry` may override this per monitor set.

layout_opts.description: Per-layout option overrides for the scene's base layout. Flat when attached to the scene's own layout, keyed by layout name for workspaces whose layout is cycled at runtime — same shape hypr/events/layout_opts.lua already consumes.

gaps.description: The scene's own gaps, taking precedence over the geometry profile. Omitted = keep the profile's gaps. Gaming sets 0/0 on both hosts, so it lives here, not in geometry.

border_size.description: Window border width on the workspace. 0 with decorate=false is how the gaming scene goes borderless on both hosts.

decorate.description: Whether the workspace renders borders/decoration at all. false + border_size 0 = the gaming scene's composite tile.

group_default.description: Grouping behavior for windows opened into this scene before `members` rules say otherwise. `always` turns the workspace into one collective tile with a groupbar (the Dofus precedent); `barred` keeps windows out of the focused group.

members.description: The scene's window set: how matching windows are identified and what each match gets. The predicate objects are the same ones hypr/windowrules.lua feeds hl.window_rule — `class`, `title`, `initial_class`, and the existing tag system ("+proton", "+gaming", ...) all address a member.

bindings.description: Binding-context tags for the scene as a whole (the which-key context tuple workspace› class› group› layout, CheatSheet.qml). A bind tagged `gaming` shows only while a gaming-scene window is focused.

reevaluate_on.description: The runtime events that must re-apply the scene. Static scene behavior is compiled at config load; this names what the event manager listens to so geometry/layout changes land without a reload — the events layout_opts/solo_gaps/opacity already hook, plus `profile.switch` (monitor set changed) and `configreloaded`.

geometry.description: How the scene differs between monitor sets. `desk-dual` is regioned (the 5120x1440 primary, a normal-aspect secondary each with its own gaps); `laptop-solo` is fit-or-float (windows fit the lid or float). Only the diverging keys are listed — the base `layout`/`gaps`/`border_size`/`decorate` hold wherever a profile says nothing.

match.description: Window-rule predicate: `class`/`initial_class`/`title` values are regex strings; `tag` addresses windows the config already tagged.

props.description: Hyprland window-rule options applied to every window this match accepts: position/size (`move`/`size`), opacity (`opacity`, e.g. "1.0 override"), blur opt-out (`no_blur`), float/tile state, grouping (`group`), fullscreen, workspace pinning (`workspace`, name-addressable so it is stable across hosts), and suppression (`suppress_event`). Values take the strings hypr rules already take; the option set stays open because Hyprland's is not this model's business to close.

bindings.description: Per-member binding-context tags, for matches that own their binds (the Dofus surface tags its keys `gaming` in CheatParse.js).

layoutOpts.description: Flat (for the scene's own layout: `{ "default_split_ratio": 1.25 }`) or nested by layout name (`{ "dwindle": {...}, "master": {...} }`). Keys must exist in the running Hyprland; layout_opts.lua validates them at config load.

profile-desktop.description: The ultrawide geometry: a 5120x1440 primary region and a normal-aspect secondary, each with its own air. Region gaps mirror hyprland.lua's `geometry_profiles`, where the secondary is the one that says so.

regions.description: Per-monitor-role constraints. `primary` is the 5120x1440 region; `secondary` the normal-aspect monitor.

profile-laptop.description: The lid geometry: no room to give away. Windows either fit the lid or float; nothing gets the desk's air.

fit_or_float.description: true = windows fit to the lid or float instead of taking a desk-width column.
